item: Catechol - redox cycling / quinone formation / covalent modification
source: PubMed PMID 27617882 (Bolton & Dunlap, Chem Res Toxicol 2016, review); PMID 19952498 (J Toxicol Sci 2009); PMID 25279998 (Penning, Chem Res Toxicol 2014, review)
note: Catechols are established substrates for oxidation to ortho-quinones (via P450/AKR or metal-catalyzed autoxidation), which are Michael acceptors that covalently modify protein thiols (e.g., Keap1) and redox-cycle to generate ROS. Directly relevant to interpreting any catechol-containing candidate as carrying an intrinsic reactive-metabolite / covalent-modification liability independent of target engagement.

item: Cyclic acyl phosphate (1,3,2-dioxaphospholan-2-one 2-oxide) - hydrolytic stability as a drug/probe
predicted_class: stable enough to survive assay buffer/cell
known_status: NOT ESTABLISHED / evidence points to instability
note: Directly relevant analog: aminoacyl PHOSPHATE ESTERS (mixed carboxylic-phosphoric anhydrides, same functional class as the candidate's acyl-phosphate ring, though acyclic) have half-lives of HOURS TO DAYS in aqueous media depending on side-chain sterics/electronics - and that is for the more hindered, less strained acyclic case. No PubMed record was found of any cyclic acyl phosphate / dioxaphospholane-2-oxide being used as a marketed drug or a bench-stable probe. General acyl-phosphate biochemistry (acetyl-phosphate, aspartyl-phosphate/E2-P of SERCA, aminoacyl-adenylates) treats this functional group as a deliberately labile high-energy intermediate, not a stable pharmacophore (see PMID 15452115 on P-O bond destabilization accelerating phosphoenzyme hydrolysis).

predicted_class: precedent for acyl-phosphate-like warheads in chemical biology
known_status: KNOWN/validated but NOT the same chemistry
source: PubMed PMID 24464431 (J Biomol Screen 2014); PMID 24187138 (J Biol Chem 2013)
note: ActivX/desthiobiotin-ATP probes covalently label a conserved active-site LYSINE via an acyl-phosphate-like electrophile on the probe's gamma-phosphate; this is a deliberately reactive, short-contact-time labeling reagent for chemoproteomics, not evidence that a cyclic acyl phosphate can survive as a stable, orally- or cell-stable inhibitor scaffold. If anything it reinforces that acyl-phosphate electrophiles are used precisely because they react quickly.

source: PubMed PMID 38954764 (Imamoto, Chem Rev 2024, review); PMID 40963379 (Wang et al., Chem Soc Rev 2025, review); PMID 41398173 (Chem Asian J 2025, review)
note: Imamoto's Chem Rev (2024) states P-stereogenic ligand chemistry 'remained a small family for many years mainly because of their synthetic difficulty' even after decades of methods development. Wang et al. 2025 (Chem Soc Rev) is specifically about stereocontrolled ProTide/oligonucleotide P-centers (sofosbuvir-class) and frames it as a persistent, non-trivial synthetic + purification challenge requiring specialized chiral auxiliaries/catalysis, not routine chemistry. A stereodefined 5-membered CYCLIC acyl-phosphate with a P-stereocenter is not covered by any of these precedents and would be an even less-precedented target.

predicted_class: established industrial precedent for one P-stereocenter class
note: Enzymatic (phosphotriesterase, engineered) kinetic resolution used to obtain pure Sp-diastereomer of remdesivir/sofosbuvir phosphoramidate precursors - i.e. even for the best-precedented P-stereocenter drug class, achieving diastereopurity required specialized biocatalyst engineering, underscoring that stereocontrol at phosphorus is a solved-but-hard problem for phosphoramidates and has no reported equivalent for cyclic acyl phosphates.

item: Pin1 phosphate-recognition pocket (Lys63/Arg68/Arg69) - direct phosphate-group ligand precedent
known_status: KNOWN/validated as ON-TARGET RATIONALE but with a documented PERMEABILITY FAILURE MODE
source: PubMed PMID 25091930 (Guo et al., Bioorg Med Chem Lett 2014, Pfizer); PMID 12721297 (Bayer et al., J Biol Chem 2003)
note: Pfizer's own SBDD series explicitly designed phosphate-based Pin1 inhibitors to engage the phosphate recognition pocket, then DELIBERATELY REPLACED the phosphate with a carboxylate and pursued further optimization specifically to improve cell permeability, arriving only then at low-micromolar cellular anti-proliferative activity. This is direct precedent that (a) a phosphate/phosphonate group in this pocket is mechanistically sensible (matches pSer/pThr-Pro recognition) but (b) phosphate groups are a recognized cell-permeability liability for Pin1 ligands in the published record, motivating replacement rather than retention. Bayer et al. 2003 measured only millimolar-range Kd for free phosphate/sulfate ion binding to Pin1's active site by fluorescence, consistent with the pocket being solvent-exposed/weak-affinity for small phosphate groups alone.
PubMed PMID 33972797 (Dubiella et al., Nat Chem Biol 2021); PMID 40546013 (Proteomics 2025); PMID 41900774 (Pharmaceutics 2026, PROTAC follow-up)
column6: Covalent Cys113-targeting electrophilic-fragment-derived Pin1 inhibitor; selective, cell- and in vivo-active, used as the warhead for subsequent Pin1-degrading PROTACs.
